cycles.method: Authored instructions only, priced at 16 core cycles each (the conservative ColdFire V4 per-instruction envelope Mute Modes' TESTING.md derives from the MCF54455 manual); not chip timing. Static: the longest path through the [PLAY] entry in patch_qlrec.s, 28 instructions (invert, PERSONALIZE screen test and redraw, reopen the toast, then stock's [PLAY] path). Measured on 0.1.1's native image (MAIN OS 3a39f682…, 23 Oct 2026): ot_emu program-counter watch on each of the unit's 35 instructions in turn, MKII panel; the longest press executed 26 (invert while live recording runs, with PERSONALIZE open and redrawn, and from a normal page). The stock routines the unit calls (project gate, checksum, menu redraw, notification open and close) are stock cost and are excluded. Budget: one 362.8 us frame at 264 MHz, used as a generous deadline for a key handler that never runs in the frame path.

load.method: Measured on 0.1.0 (20 Oct 2026), not repeated for 0.1.1, whose unit differs only in the flip (store order, PERSONALIZE screen test) and runs only on key presses. Emulator, not hardware: ot_emu --mkii --dsp (the ColdFire port, built from the upstream:tools Octabam checkout 67e5ea37; the binary Apply Scene's measurements used), frame engine on, 20 Oct 2026. Two native static-stock images from this source: CF METER + CF METER IDLE + the stock effects (upstream Octabam's probe, private, not in Modwerk), and the same plus this module; the same project (Apply Scene's perf fixture, T8 FX2 = CF METER), transport playing, crossfader 64, 10 s of the same MIDI flood on both (one three-byte message per ms: notes on and off and CCs on channels 1-8 and 11, about 1,000 a second, plus clock at 240 BPM), and the same keys on both about every 1.1 s: hold [REC], tap [PLAY], tap [PLAY] again, release [REC] (10 gestures; on this module's image each showed the toast and flipped the setting, 10 flips; on both images the first one started live recording). Longest frame interrupt: the largest per-cycle 'isr max' that tools/harness/cfmeter.py --dump (upstream Octabam's decoder) reads from five 2 s cycles, in the port's own time (it prices each instruction at one step, so these microseconds are not the unit's). Idle: CF METER IDLE reads 0 % on both images because the port fast-forwards main's idle park, so idle is the port's own share instead: 100 x (1 - executed instructions / (3,990 instructions per sample x elapsed samples)) over the run. The same flood without the gesture: longest 129.3 us stock, 129.2 us with the module, idle 62.38 % both (the module costs nothing between presses). With the gesture both images reach 149.5-149.6 us (live recording and the key handling are stock's; the module adds no frame-interrupt work) and idle is 0.27 points lower with the module (its toast, checksum and menu-redraw calls run in the key handler, outside the interrupt).

stress.droppedExplanation: Measured on 0.1.0 (20 Oct 2026), not repeated for 0.1.1. Emulator, not hardware: ot_emu --mkii --dsp, this module's image and project above, 62 s of the flood (62,068 three-byte messages and 5,960 clocks), transport playing; at 7, 22, 37 and 52 s STOP with a note held on channel 1 (which also ends live recording), then Part 2, PLAY and Part 1 (the Part changed by calling stock's own selection routine 0x4004a8a4, as Apply Scene did, because PART + TRIG did not change it in the port's panel script; once the port refused the call because main was busy and it succeeded 50 ms later); the gesture (hold [REC], [PLAY], [PLAY], release [REC]) every 2.5 s between, 24 times, 24 flips. Dropped: counted at the MIDI thread's handlers (note on, note off, CC, clock, start, stop); every type's handler entries were at least the messages sent (up to three more than sent on some types, one or two on the stock image under the same input: the PC watch counting an entry twice, not extra input), and none were missing. Stuck notes: nothing was sent to MIDI OUT, and the firmware's per-channel note bookkeeping at the end is identical to the stock image's under the same input and keys; no samples are loaded and no MIDI track plays notes in this project, so audible stuck notes could not occur here. Hangs: frames advanced to the end and a gesture after the final STOP reached the [PLAY] handler and opened the toast. MIDI START, CONTINUE and STOP (transport receive on) run their own handlers and never reached the [PLAY] key handler 0x40061778 or the module (0 entries in three rounds; a panel [PLAY] tap: 1), so the flood does not run this module's code. Bypass and MIDI channel changes do not apply: the module has no bypass and no MIDI path.

hardwareEvidence.note: Functional checks on the author's unit, nothing timed or recorded (TESTING.md, Hardware report). The load and stress rows above are ot_emu measurements of 0.1.0.
